name: templates-dir-validation
body: Templates dir validation: before any deck validation, render or serve (startup and every reload), kalide validates the resolved library root (the configured `templates:` path, else the local `templates/`; see external-template-library) — the loader's single resolution point — fail-fast in a fixed order: (1) `library.yaml` present and valid; (2) structure (templates-dir-layout: the library structure is library.yaml, slides/, sections/, themes/ and media/, and its template names are unique across slides/ and sections/. Every other top-level entry is ignored — the loader validates only the library itself, so a `.git/` directory, a README, a root-level `AGENTS.md` (library-guide-layout) or any other unrelated entry loads cleanly and stays inert: it is never parsed, validated, rendered, listed or served); (3) each template in kind-then-name order (slides/ then sections/): `template.yaml`, `layout.html.tmpl`, `example.md` present, `template.yaml` well-formed against the schema vocabulary (no `usage:` key), layout parses as standard html/template with the documented function set (template-language), parse errors file:line-qualified; (4) the template-build-checks across the set (requirements.constraint.template-registry-integrity); (5) each theme in name order has `theme.css`; (6) references resolve: in a theme's `theme.css` — and in every CSS it `@import`s from within that theme's own directory — each `@import` directive is followed in either form, the quoted-string form `@import "x.css";` and the `url()` form `@import url("x.css");`; an `@import` target is resolved relative to the importing CSS file, is a relative path inside that theme's own directory, and names an existing file there; imports are followed bounded and cycle-safe, so an import cycle or an import escaping the theme directory is a templates error; an `@import` target carrying the reserved `media:` prefix or any other scheme — e.g. `@import url('media:x.css')` or `@import 'media:x.css'` — is a templates error naming the offending CSS file and line: the reserved `media:` prefix is valid only for a `url(…)` reference *within* the served CSS (the imported file lives under `media/` and is not served from the theme route, so it would otherwise be neither validated nor rewritten); in the served CSS every relative url(…) resolves to an existing file inside that theme's directory (`themes/<name>/` under the resolved root), and a url(…) carrying the reserved `media:` prefix resolves to an existing file under the resolved library's `media/` (the path after the prefix is relative to `media/` and stays within it) exactly like a layout `media "path"` argument; every other scheme (http:, data:, //, …), an absolute path and a `..` escape in theme CSS are rejected with a templates error naming the offending CSS file and line; every relative src/href in layouts resolves to an existing file inside the resolved library; and every `media "path"` argument in a layout is a relative path inside `media/` naming an existing file under the resolved library's `media/` — a violation is a templates error qualified with the layout's file:line (requirements.constraint.media-paths-library-relative); (7) each example.md validates against its template and its layout executes (execute errors file:line-qualified). The first failure is reported as a templates error: path-qualified (e.g. `<library>/slides/content/template.yaml:12`), with a hint and closest-match suggestion where applicable, in the terminal at startup and in the full-page error on reload — the same error-reporting format as deck errors, labelled as a templates error. AC: one test per step shows the expected first error (step 6 includes a missing `media` file, a `..` argument and an absolute argument, a `media:` theme-CSS reference to a missing file and one with a `..` or absolute path, a reserved-`media:` `@import` target in both forms — `@import url('media:x.css')` and `@import 'media:x.css'` — reported as a templates error naming the CSS file and line, and an `@import` cycle or escaping import); a valid dir proceeds to deck validation.
